entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aristaeus of Croton (b. 450 BCE, Crotone) was a philosopher or thinker of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Crotone.

He was a key figure in the development of Stoicism, a school of thought that emphasized reason, self-control, and indifference to external events.

Aristaeus' teachings were influenced by the ideas of his contemporaries, including the physician Hippocrates and the philosopher Plato.

He is considered one of the most important figures in the history of Stoicism, and his ideas continue to be studied and debated by scholars today.

Aristaeus' legacy can be seen in the many Stoic schools and communities that flourished in the ancient world, including the famous Stoic gymnasium in Athens.

In 500 BCE, Aristaeus of Croton died, leaving behind a lasting impact on the development of Western philosophy.

"Reason is the queen of the world," Aristaeus once said, a quote that encapsulates the Stoic emphasis on rational inquiry and self-reliance.

Aristaeus of Croton's contributions to the field of philosophy have had a profound and lasting impact on Western thought.
